text: dsh-persona-slot 是面向 DSH Web 和 TUI 的人设插件，通过 system-prompt/assemble 钩子把人设加入模型提示词。它按会话独立设置人设，并支持通配和全局默认；用户可用 /persona 命令管理，也可在 Web 的已安装插件面板编辑总人设、查看活动会话并调整追加或替换模式。运行时改动会持久保存到本机 DSH_HOME 目录。
dsh-persona-slot assigns a prompt persona per DSH session, with wildcard and global fallbacks. Use /persona to edit it; the Web Installed-page panel also manages defaults and shows live sessions.
我想让不同的 DSH 会话分别使用不同角色设定。
能不能给所有会话设一个默认人设，同时允许个别会话覆盖？
How can I change a conversation's persona while DSH is running?
dsh-persona-slot 的功能「按会话注入人设」：它先查当前会话的人设，再查通配人设和全局人设，并把找到的文本加入该会话的系统提示词。可用 /persona set 更新，变更从下一次模型步骤生效。
dsh-persona-slot 的功能「Web 人设面板」：在已安装插件页编辑全局或通配人设、查看活动会话当前解析的人设，并清除会话覆盖或选择追加、替换模式。面板通过插件提供的 HTTP 路由读取状态和提交修改。

dsh-persona-slot README · dsh-persona-slot：Per-session persona slot for DeepSeek Harness. Every session holds **exactly one** persona — writing a new one replaces the old instead of layering — and one global persona covers every session that has no persona of its own. Persona length is unbounded. Edit either from the conversation with `/persona`, or from the panel under **Plugins → Installed**.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

dsh-persona-slot README · Why this exists：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` gives one persona to a whole preset. That is the right tool when every session of a preset should be the same character. It cannot answer the other two questions:

- *This* session should be a cat, and that one should be a lawyer — at the same time, in the same window.
- The persona should be changeable while the conversation is already running.

dsh-persona-slot README · Why this exists：This plugin answers both. It resolves a persona per session from three tiers and applies it through one agent-scoped prompt hook, so two sessions never see each other's choice and a change takes effect on the next model step.

dsh-persona-slot README · One persona per session：That is a guarantee, not a convention:

- A session's store record is single-valued; `set` replaces, so a third write overwrites the second and never concatenates.
- Resolution returns at the first tier that holds a record, so an exact-session persona and the global persona never both reach one prompt.
- `one persona per session` and `a session never resolves two personas at once` pin both rules in the unit suite.

dsh-persona-slot README · Resolution order：The first tier that holds a record wins.

| Order | Tier | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | exact session id | `config.sessions["<id>"]` or the runtime store |
| 2 | wildcard `"*"` | `config.sessions["*"]` or the runtime store |
| 3 | global | `config.global` or the runtime store |

dsh-persona-slot README · Resolution order：A record is either text — used as the persona — or an explicit blank, which **mutes** that tier. With `blankOverrides: true` (the default) a blank stops the lookup, so a session can silence itself without deleting the deployment default. With `blankOverrides: false` a blank falls through to the next tier.

dsh-persona-slot README · Install：```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-persona-slot
```

Local development:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-persona-slot
```

The bundle patch mounts one row, `persona-slot`.

dsh-persona-slot README · Configure：```yaml
- id: persona-slot
  config:
    # Persona every session inherits.
    global: "You are a terse systems engineer. Answer in short commands."

dsh-persona-slot README · Configure：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `global` | `""` | Persona every session inherits |
| `sessions` | `{}` | Per-session personas; `"*"` is the wildcard tier |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; `false` injects nothing and keeps stored text |
| `mode` | `append` | `append` adds a section, `replace` rewrites the deployment persona |
| `prefix` | `""` | Text written above the persona |
| `suffix` | `""` | Text written below the persona |
| `blankOverrides` | `true` | Whether a blank record mutes its tier instead of falling through |
| `includeSubagents` | `true` | Whether subagent sessions also resolve a persona |
dsh-persona-slot README · Configure：`mode` can also be changed at runtime with `/persona mode`.

dsh-persona-slot README · The Installed-page panel：In the Web GUI open **Plugins → Installed** and find `dsh-persona-slot`. Its `persona-slot` row is now expandable: the arrow opens this plugin's own page, which owns:

dsh-persona-slot README · The Installed-page panel：- **Global persona (总人设)** — a multi-line editor; saving it applies to every session without its own persona from the next model step.
- **Wildcard persona** — for sessions that have no persona of their own.
- **Placement** — append after the deployment persona, replace it, or follow profile config.
- **Live sessions** — each live session's resolved persona, where it came from, and a Clear control for sessions holding their own.

dsh-persona-slot README · The Installed-page panel：The panel refreshes every ten seconds and never overwrites text you have typed but not saved.

It talks to the plugin's own `/persona-slot/state` and `/persona-slot/update` routes instead of the settings form, because that form's value field is single-line and cannot hold a character sheet. A panel save and a `/persona set` in a session write the same document, so the two never disagree.

dsh-persona-slot README · The `/persona` command：```text
/persona                             show this session's resolved persona
/persona show [this|global|all]      show one target
/persona set <text>                  set this session's persona
/persona set global <text>           set the persona every session inherits

Text is taken verbatim, multi-line included. A session id is only recognised after `for`, so `/persona set 你是猫娘` sets the persona to "你是猫娘" instead of treating it as a target.

dsh-persona-slot README · Where the runtime state lives：`$DSH_HOME/persona-slot/personas.json`

Profile configuration is a deployment default; this file is what the user typed. Keeping them apart means a plugin upgrade, a profile rebuild, or a reinstall never erases a persona written in a session. A malformed file is moved aside as `personas.json.corrupt` and the plugin starts empty instead of failing.

dsh-persona-slot README · How it hooks in：In `append` mode the persona becomes a `persona-slot:session` section placed right after the deployment persona. In `replace` mode the deployment persona section itself is rewritten. Persona text is marked `interpolate: false`, so a literal `{{anything}}` in a persona survives prompt assembly instead of being treated as an unresolved variable.

dsh-persona-slot README · What the model sees：One additional prompt section (`append`) or a rewritten deployment persona (`replace`) holding the operator's persona text. The section is stable across steps until the persona changes, so provider prompt caching keeps working between edits.
dsh-persona-slot README · Token effect：The persona text plus the section separator (a blank line). Nothing else is added.

dsh-persona-slot README · KV Cache effect：An unchanged persona keeps the prefix stable. A `/persona set` changes the prefix, which invalidates the cache from that section onward; that is the intended cost of changing an identity mid-conversation.

dsh-persona-slot README · Known limitations：- **Not a security boundary.** Personas are prompt text the operator writes. They do not restrict tools, sandbox mode, or approval policy — use those for enforcement.
- **The panel needs an HTTP surface.** The routes are registered on `ctx.webServer`, so a headless or TUI composition has only the `/persona` command.
- **No persona-length ceiling.** A very long persona is sent on every request and consumes context; that cost is the operator's to budget.
- **Session ids, not titles.** Overrides key on the session id. A resumed or forked session keeps the id, so its persona follows it; a title change does not move a persona.
- **One persona per session.** Two personas cannot be layered on one session; combine them into one text.
- **`replace` needs a deployment persona slot.** It rewrites `deployment:persona-prefix`. If a composition mounted `dsh-persona` inside a preset without that section, `replace` still inserts the section at the front of the assembled prompt, so the session is never left without one.

dsh-persona-slot README · Supported DSH versions：`0.2.1-rc.2` through `0.2.1-rc.5`, declared as
`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.2.1-0 || >=0.2.1-rc.1 <=0.2.1-rc.5`.

dsh-persona-slot README · Supported DSH versions：The range is written out in explicit prerelease branches on purpose. node-semver
only lets a prerelease version satisfy a range when some comparator in that range
sits on the same `major.minor.patch` tuple and carries a prerelease tag of its
own, so a broad-looking `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` silently excludes every
`0.2.1-*` build — including the ones this plugin is tested on. The explicit
branches keep `0.2.1-rc.1` … `rc.5` inside and leave `0.2.1` itself, the alpha
builds, and `0.3.0-*` outside.

dsh-persona-slot README · Supported DSH versions：Developed and tested against `0.2.1-rc.2`; the release builds are the same host
packages with patch-level fixes, and the plugin only uses the stable seams
(`agents`, `commands`, `systemPrompt`, `webServer`).

dsh-persona-slot README · Development：```bash
npm test          # unit tests + real-runtime integration test
npm run check     # syntax check every module
```

The integration test boots a real Cordis composition (`dsh-system-prompt`, `dsh-agent`, `dsh-agent-loop`, `dsh-commands`, `dsh-session`, `dsh-tools`) and asserts that two sessions assemble different prompts. Set `DSH_HOST_ROOT` to the `@deepseek-ai` host package directory to run it; the suite skips rather than fails when that runtime is absent.
